# A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models

## Research question

Independent SQL samples can repeat one reading of an ambiguous request while missing other valid interpretations.

## Method

PoolDPP draws candidate strings, combines language-model likelihood with normalized embedding geometry, and selects a fixed-size set using a determinantal point process. Stochastic selection uses importance correction; greedy MAP targets the best subset of the observed pool.

## Evaluation

The SQL experiment uses Gemma-2-9B, MiniLM-L6, 100 AMBROSIA questions, 100 pools of 200 candidates and three selected queries. Recall counts annotated interpretations matched by execution; precision requires an entire result match. FineWeb and mathematical reasoning supply additional tests.

## What the results support

At reported high-recall settings, both variants improve AMBROSIA recall over ancestral sampling while reducing precision. Question-paired tests do not resolve recall gains over K-means. The largest tested pool-coverage mean is 41.8%; selection cannot recover absent interpretations.

## Limits and qualifications

SQL evidence comes from one model and a small fixed subset. Temperature selection and proposal coverage matter; likelihood, embeddings and finite database results are imperfect semantic proxies. Pool generation dominates cost. The conditional KL theorem concerns target-to-average stochastic output, not each realized pool, MAP or SQL correctness; numerical bounds use restricted pool-built instances. Repository documentation leaves some early-run settings unrecorded. No independent execution or proof checking was performed.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful adjacent evidence for constructing interpretation sets, with precision and pool-coverage limits; it does not implement clarification, abstention or user-intent recovery.
